paragraphs.text: The impurity of her infirmity: the days of a woman's monthly period.

Bearing children was a blessing and a divine command before the Fall. But after the Fall and the curse, bearing offspring became the bearing of sinful children who carry the sin of Adam and Eve. So childbirth was counted as an uncleanness, so that the woman might remember her sins and so that it might be an occasion for repentance. And because whatever she touches would be unclean, this calls her to complete rest, which helps her regain her health after the labors of childbirth. The woman who gives birth is unclean for seven days if she bears a male child.
Foreskin: a small piece of skin that is removed from the child's male organ.

The newborn is circumcised on the eighth day so that he may become a member of the people of God. His nature is renewed on the eighth day, which signifies eternity, where he receives a spiritual nature fit for the Kingdom. And because circumcision is a type of Baptism, which gives us new life in Christ and prepares us for the Kingdom of Heaven, it is no longer necessary to perform it in the New Testament, and when Christians do it, it is for health reasons only.
The sanctuary: the tabernacle of meeting.

The blood of her purifying: the blood that comes after childbirth. Blood is the basis of life, and its flowing points to the death that came upon man because of sin. So in the Old Testament it was considered an uncleanness and required a period of purification; but in the New Testament, through the death of Christ and the shedding of His blood, we receive cleansing from our sins, and the flow of blood is not considered an uncleanness. The woman remained in her uncleanness for the following thirty-three days, so that the whole period was forty days from the birth. She was not to touch anything holy or come to the house of the Lord. In the New Testament, Christ has lifted uncleanness from woman and from all His people by His salvation; yet she cannot partake of the Holy Mysteries, because of the lack of fitness and bodily cleanliness. The Law set forty days so that the effects of the flow of blood would end for all women, even those who take longer than others.

The period is doubled in the case of the birth of a female child, so that the mother may remember that the woman fell into sin before the man, tempted him, and afterward caused him to fall into sin. So the mother offers a doubled repentance for herself, not for the baby girl, so that she may live with God in depth and encourage her husband to the spiritual life.

Celebrate the feast of your Baptism at every baptism you attend, just as you celebrate your birthday, because Baptism is the beginning of your spiritual life, your sonship to God, and your worthiness to inherit eternal life. Remember that you have received a new nature, so that you may live to God in all your thoughts, words and deeds, and not to the world.
A lamb of the first year: one year old.
A young pigeon: a small dove.

We notice that the sacrifice is one and the same for the newborn, male or female, a sign of the equality of the two sexes in God's sight (Gal 3:28, Col 3:11). And the pairing of the burnt offering and the sin offering, which are the lamb and the young pigeon, shows the double work of Christ in:
1- Pleasing the Father (the burnt offering).
2- Paying the price of the sins of humanity (the sin offering).
The fountain of her blood: the blood that was flowing from the woman who had given birth.

Offering the burnt offering and the sin offering for the woman who has given birth cleanses her from the blood that was flowing from her after childbirth, and this is a type of the blood of Christ, which cleanses us in the sacraments of Baptism, confession and Communion. The blood that a woman sheds is a symbol of the death that came upon the human race because of sin. Death was considered an uncleanness, and whoever touched the dead became unclean; likewise blood was considered an uncleanness. But Christ by His blood took away our sins, so that the blood a woman sheds in the New Testament is not considered an uncleanness but a health ailment.

The poor could substitute a young dove or a young turtledove for the lamb of the burnt offering. This was the sacrifice of the Virgin Mary, who fulfilled the rite in spite of the purity of her childbirth, so that her humility and her fulfilling of the Law might be clear to us. The Virgin was a human being upon whom lay the sin of Adam and Eve, and she was not conceived without stain, so she needed purification through the sacrifices that signify the sacrifice of Christ her Savior. We notice that the sin offering is a turtledove or a young pigeon, a cheap bird, to take away the sin of the woman who has given birth; but the burnt offering is according to the financial means of the woman giving birth: either a lamb, or a turtledove, or a young pigeon.

Let us remember Him who became poor for our sake, though He is the source of all riches, so that we may thank Him abundantly, and so that all the material things of the world and their wealth may become small in our eyes. Then we shall not grow weary from material hardship, or bodily weakness, or any problems that pass over us, because our God is strong, and our Redeemer will deliver us from them all and comfort our hearts during these afflictions.
Leprosy of persons and of garments: introduction
Leprosy is a contagious skin disease that disfigures the body; it existed in the Old Testament.

Leprosy was connected with sin and might be a punishment for it, as in the case of Miriam the sister of Moses (Num 12:10-15), Gehazi the disciple of the prophet Elisha (2 Kgs 5:27), and King Uzziah (2 Chr 26:19-23). The priest would diagnose the disease and then confirm that it had gone, after the sick person had been separated for a period of time from mixing with the people. When he was healed of the disease, he offered sacrifices through the priest, and God forgave him his sins.
There was no cure for this disease, but healing comes from God. The healing is called cleansing, because it is deliverance from the effects of sin.
(a) Leprosy of persons (vv. 1-46). It includes various symptoms that reveal the presence of the disease, which are:

(1) White hair (vv. 1-3). 1 And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron, saying, 2 “When a man shall have in the skin of his flesh a rising, a scab, or bright spot, and it be in the skin of his flesh like the plague of leprosy; then he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest, or unto one of his sons the priests: 3 And the priest shall look on the plague in the skin of the flesh: and when the hair in the plague is turned white, and the plague in sight be deeper than the skin of his flesh, it is a plague of leprosy: and the priest shall look on him, and pronounce him unclean.”
The Lord spoke to Moses because he was the leader of the people, and to Aaron because he was the high priest, responsible with his sons for carrying out the Law.
A rising: a swelling, a tumor, or the mark of a wound.
A scab: a skin eruption.
A bright spot: a patch on the skin of a different color.

If a raised part, or a red or shining white part, was noticed on the skin of any Jewish person, they would bring him to the priest so that he might examine it and know whether these were signs of leprosy or of another skin disease.

The examination was held between the sixth hour and the ninth hour by Jewish reckoning, that is, from twelve to three in the afternoon, when the light of the sun is strong. The sick person's coming to the priest is a symbol of the sinner's turning to the father of confession to repent, so that the priest may examine his sins and guide him to the means of curing sin. The examination was not made on the Sabbath, because it is a day set apart for worship, so it was put off to the following day; and if the priest wished, he could seek the help of some experienced persons from among the people to diagnose the disease.

The priest examines him. If he finds in the discolored skin hair that has turned white, and also a depression in the skin, he is sure that it is the disease of leprosy, and he orders that the person be declared unclean and isolated.

If strange thoughts war against you and you doubt yourself, then turn to your father of confession and disclose your thoughts to him, and God will guide you through his tongue, so that you may resist the deceiving devil, repel the thoughts, and fortify yourself with the means of grace as your spiritual father guides you.

(2) The bright spot (vv. 4-8). 4 “If the bright spot be white in the skin of his flesh, and in sight be not deeper than the skin, and the hair thereof be not turned white; then the priest shall shut up him that hath the plague seven days: 5 And the priest shall look on him the seventh day: and, behold, if the plague in his sight be at a stay, and the plague spread not in the skin; then the priest shall shut him up seven days more: 6 And the priest shall look on him again the seventh day: and, behold, if the plague be somewhat dark, and the plague spread not in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean: it is but a scab: and he shall wash his clothes, and be clean. 7 But if the scab spread much abroad in the skin, after that he hath been seen of the priest for his cleansing, he shall be seen of the priest again: 8 And if the priest see that, behold, the scab spreadeth in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a leprosy.”

The second symptom that the disease of leprosy may have is the appearance of a white spot in the skin, but without white hair in it and without a depression in the skin. This symptom may be leprosy or a similar skin disease, so the priest shuts him up with him for seven days, to make sure first whether the disease advances and other symptoms appear. The confinement was in tents near the tabernacle of meeting in the wilderness of Sinai, or in side rooms of the Temple in Jerusalem. The elders of the Jews did not shut up a suspected person on his wedding day or during the feasts of Unleavened Bread and Tabernacles.
In his sight: as the priest sees it.
If after seven days the priest notices that the white spot has not increased, he shuts him up for another seven days to be sure.
Dark: its color is deep.
Scab: a mark that is not harmful to the skin.

If after the second seven days the priest notices that the spot has not increased but its color has become darker, it is not leprosy; so he pronounces him clean, because this is merely a mark on the skin and not leprosy.
If after seven days the priest notices that the spots on the skin have increased, he shuts him up another seven days to make sure that it is the disease of leprosy.
If the priest notices that the spots on the skin have spread and increased, he judges that it is the disease of leprosy and orders the sick person to be isolated because of his uncleanness.

Do not be hasty in your judgments, lest you wrong another. Ask for God's guidance, think calmly, and seek counsel from the spiritual fathers as much as you can, especially in big decisions, and be confident that God will value your prayer and your turning to Him and will guide you to what is for your good and the good of others.

(3) White spots with raw flesh in them (vv. 9-11). 9 “When the plague of leprosy is in a man, then he shall be brought unto the priest; 10 And the priest shall see him: and, behold, if the rising be white in the skin, and it have turned the hair white, and there be quick raw flesh in the rising; 11 It is an old leprosy in the skin of his flesh, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean, and shall not shut him up: for he is unclean.”

The third case of leprosy is the presence of white spots higher than the ordinary skin, that is, a swelling, with white hair in it, but inside these white spots there are portions of living flesh, that is, the natural color of the body's flesh. In this case the priest judges that it is the disease of leprosy and isolates the sick person because of his uncleanness. This symptom declares that the disease of leprosy is of long standing in the sick person, that is, chronic, and so he is certainly unclean.

Do not be lenient with sin until it becomes deep in you and you grow accustomed to it, and you need greater striving to be rid of it. Cut off the sources of sin from the beginning and confess it, and you will be cleansed of it quickly with little striving.

The fourth case in the appearance of the disease of leprosy is the spreading of the white spots until they cover the whole body, that is, the whole skin becomes white. This means that the course of the disease is complete and the skin will return to its natural color, so the priest pronounces him clean. Spiritually, this signifies that the sick person has felt his complete lack, repented and humbled himself, and so deserves forgiveness and healing.

If the leprosy spreads and covers the whole body, but the priest discovers the presence of even small portions of living flesh, that is, the natural color of the body, among the white, he judges him leprous and unclean. Spiritually, this signifies wavering between a life of purity and uncleanness, or between good and evil.

In the last case mentioned in (vv. 14, 15), if the portions that were the color of living flesh change and become white, that is, the whole body becomes white, it is like the case mentioned in (vv. 12, 13), and he is pronounced clean.
Try to remain steadfast in your spiritual path and in carrying out your rule of prayer, so that you may abide in life with God and receive forgiveness, for the wavering person is unclean before God.
The case here arose as a mark in the skin after an abscess or boil that left a white sign tending to redness, or a raised mark, so he is brought to the priest.

The priest examines the sick person. If he finds in the mark of the boil a depression in the skin with white hair in it, he knows that it is the disease of leprosy and pronounces him unclean; that is, he finds in the place of the boil some parts raised in the skin and other parts depressed.

If by examination the priest finds that the place of the boil is a dark-colored spot, with no depression in the skin or white hair, he shuts him up seven days to be sure whether it is the disease of leprosy or not, because these signs are not sufficient to diagnose leprosy.
If the priest notices that the spot spreads in the skin, it is the disease of leprosy, and he pronounces the sick person unclean.
If the spot that is in the mark of the boil does not spread, it is merely a mark of it and not one of the symptoms of leprosy, so the priest pronounces him clean.

If you have repented of a sin, do not keep traces of it in your life, such as an evil friend, bad pictures, or any matters that had a connection with sin. Rather, get rid of all of it firmly, lest it bring you back to worse sins.
Keep away from the sources of sin and cling to the Church, and you will be steadfast in the life of repentance.

(6) A burning of fire (vv. 24-28). 24 “Or if there be any flesh, in the skin whereof there is a hot burning, and the quick flesh that burneth have a white bright spot, somewhat reddish, or white; 25 Then the priest shall look upon it: and, behold, if the hair in the bright spot be turned white, and it be in sight deeper than the skin; it is a leprosy broken out of the burning: wherefore the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy. 26 But if the priest look on it, and, behold, there be no white hair in the bright spot, and it be no lower than the other skin, but be somewhat dark; then the priest shall shut him up seven days: 27 And the priest shall look upon him the seventh day: and if it be spread much abroad in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy. 28 And if the bright spot stay in his place, and spread not in the skin, but it be somewhat dark; it is a rising of the burning, and the priest shall pronounce him clean: for it is an inflammation of the burning.”
"The quick flesh that burneth": the skin that has been renewed in the place of the burn.
Treatment by cauterizing was used anciently, but after the skin grows back in the place of the burn, its color may be white or white tending to redness.
This must be shown to the priest so that he may examine it for the three signs of leprosy explained above, which are:
a depression in the surface of the skin, whiteness of the hair, and spreading. If he finds them, he pronounces the sick person unclean.
There may remain only a mark of the burn of a color darker than the color of the skin, so the sick person is isolated for seven days so that the priest may be sure of his cleanness.
If the mark spreads, it was leprosy; but if it does not spread, it is merely a mark of the burn, which is harmless.

Pray much that God may remove the trace of the wars of lust from your heart, so that you do not desire your old sins lest you be burned by their fire once again. Resist evil thoughts by repeating prayers, however long the thoughts continue, and be confident that God rejoices in this striving of yours, for it is evidence of your repentance, and He upholds you until you are rid of them and come out of this war with a stronger spiritual will and spiritual growth.

(7) A plague on the head or beard (vv. 29-37). 29 “If a man or woman have a plague upon the head or the beard; 30 Then the priest shall see the plague: and, behold, if it be in sight deeper than the skin; and there be in it a yellow thin hair; then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a dry scall, even a leprosy upon the head or beard. 31 And if the priest look on the plague of the scall, and, behold, it be not in sight deeper than the skin, and that there is no black hair in it; then the priest shall shut up him that hath the plague of the scall seven days: 32 And in the seventh day the priest shall look on the plague: and, behold, if the scall spread not, and there be in it no yellow hair, and the scall be not in sight deeper than the skin; 33 He shall be shaven, but the scall shall he not shave; and the priest shall shut up him that hath the scall seven days more: 34 And in the seventh day the priest shall look on the scall: and, behold, if the scall be not spread in the skin, nor in sight deeper than the skin; then the priest shall pronounce him clean: and he shall wash his clothes, and be clean. 35 But if the scall spread much in the skin after his cleansing; 36 Then the priest shall look on him: and, behold, if the scall be spread in the skin, the priest shall not seek for yellow hair; he is unclean. 37 But if the scall be in his sight at a stay, and that there is black hair grown up therein; the scall is healed, he is clean: and the priest shall pronounce him clean.”
Plague: an abnormal sign.

The skin disease may be in the head or beard of a man or a woman. As the Apostle Paul says that the head of the man is Christ, a plague in the head of a man signifies a weakness or defect that has afflicted his faith in Christ; but the head of the woman is the man, so a plague in the head of a woman signifies a defect in her relationship with her husband. As for the beard, it signifies dignity and honor, so a plague in it signifies the effect of sins in dishonoring a person's spiritual dignity.
Yellow: of a yellow color.

Thin: fine (weak). Scall: a scalp disease (a contagious skin disease). If the priest notices a depression of the skin and the presence of yellow hair, he pronounces the sick person unclean, because it is the disease of leprosy, which has appeared in the form of a scall on the head or beard.

If the priest notices that the skin is not depressed but the hair is not black and its color has changed, this means that some of the signs have disappeared, so isolation for seven days is called for, to be deliberate in judgment, and the lack of spreading is a sign that calls for further confirmation.

The priest shaves the place around the plague so that it appears clearly, and shuts up the sick person, isolated, for another seven days. If it is established that it has not spread, he is clean, and he washes his clothes as a confirmation of his cleanness.
But if the spots spread in the skin and the priest notices this after shutting him up seven days, it means that it is leprosy, and he pronounces him unclean even if he finds no yellow hair.

The sick person is not counted clean unless the spreading of the disease has stopped and black hair, that is, strong and sound hair, has reappeared. This signifies the person's return to his spiritual strength, and so he is clean.
Keep up the means of grace to be rid of every weakness that befalls you because of sin, and regular Communion is among the most important of these strengthening means.

(8) The freckled spot (vv. 38, 39). 38 “If a man also or a woman have in the skin of their flesh bright spots, even white bright spots; 39 Then the priest shall look: and, behold, if the bright spots in the skin of their flesh be darkish white; it is a freckled spot that groweth in the skin; he is clean.”
Bright spots, bright spots: patches, patches.
Freckled spot: this is the disease of vitiligo, which appears in the form of white patches on the skin, and it is not contagious.

If the priest finds a person with dark white patches on his skin, that is, not pure white, and there are no other signs in the skin, this is not leprosy but the disease of vitiligo, so he pronounces him clean.

Do not be hasty in judging people, for they may have an appearance that you think is connected with sin .. Be patient in judgment, for they may be pure, and do not busy yourself much with judging others, but look only for virtues, make excuses for mistakes, and pray for everyone, and for yourself before them.

(9) Baldness (vv. 40-44). 40 “And the man whose hair is fallen off his head, he is bald; yet is he clean. 41 And he that hath his hair fallen off from the part of his head toward his face, he is forehead bald: yet is he clean. 42 And if there be in the bald head, or bald forehead, a white reddish sore; it is a leprosy sprung up in his bald head, or his bald forehead. 43 Then the priest shall look upon it: and, behold, if the rising of the sore be white reddish in his bald head, or in his bald forehead, as the leprosy appeareth in the skin of the flesh; 44 He is a leprous man, he is unclean: the priest shall pronounce him utterly unclean; his plague is in his head.”
Bald: the falling out of all the hair of the head.
Forehead bald: the falling out of the hair from the front of the head only.
The condition here is not a disease, whether through the falling out of all the hair of the head or the hair from the front of the head only.
But the appearance of the symptoms of leprosy in the head establishes the person's uncleanness, and they are white spots tending to redness.

Having any lack in you in material respects, such as poverty or sickness, is no disgrace to you, provided it is not accompanied by any symptoms of sin, that is, the lack does not lead to grumbling, or resentment of others, or any bad treatment. Accept your inability and your weakness, do not compare yourself with anyone, and be confident that God will make you complete, and you will be in fullness and spiritual happiness.

(10) The law of the leper (vv. 45, 46). 45 “And the leper in whom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, and his head bare, and he shall put a covering upon his upper lip, and shall cry, Unclean, unclean. 46 All the days wherein the plague shall be in him he shall be defiled; he is unclean: he shall dwell alone; without the camp shall his habitation be.”
The camp: the place where the people's tents were set up.
The leper is obliged to do five things once his infection with leprosy is established, which are:

1- He rends his clothes, and this signifies the exposure of sin, since the body of the one afflicted with the disease is shown; note that this applied to men only and not to women, out of regard for their modesty.
2- Baring the head, that is, not wearing a turban or the like, and this signifies his loss of dignity because of sin.
3- The man covering his upper lip, as a symbol of his loss of his spiritual manliness because of his weakness and his fall into sin.
4- He cries out about himself that he is unclean, and this means his confession of his sin, and also that no one may come near him and touch him and so make others unclean.
5- He is isolated from the place where people dwell, as a symbol of his loss of his communion in the Church.

All these duties help the sick person to repent and reject all his old sins, so that God may have compassion on him and heal him of his disease. Leprosy is a disease that indicates the uncleanness of man, and it has symptoms as already explained in this chapter. God allows this disease because of man's falling into great sins, and there is no healing from this disease by drugs or any medical treatment; healing comes from God, confirming that this disease is connected with sin and its cure is repentance.

Take care to confess your sins and humble yourself before God, and do not be angry if your father of confession gives you a discipline such as deprivation from Communion, for all this helps you to repent, so that you receive God's mercies and regain your spiritual strength.

(b) Leprosy of garments (vv. 47-59). 47 “The garment also that the plague of leprosy is in, whether it be a woollen garment, or a linen garment; 48 Whether it be in the warp, or woof; of linen, or of woollen; whether in a skin, or in any thing made of skin; 49 And if the plague be greenish or reddish in the garment, or in the skin, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in any thing of skin; it is a plague of leprosy, and shall be shewed unto the priest: 50 And the priest shall look upon the plague, and shut up it that hath the plague seven days: 51 And he shall look on the plague on the seventh day: if the plague be spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in a skin, or in any work that is made of skin; the plague is a fretting leprosy; it is unclean. 52 He shall therefore burn that garment, whether warp or woof, in woollen or in linen, or any thing of skin, wherein the plague is: for it is a fretting leprosy; it shall be burnt in the fire. 53 And if the priest shall look, and, behold, the plague be not spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in any thing of skin; 54 Then the priest shall command that they wash the thing wherein the plague is, and he shall shut it up seven days more: 55 And the priest shall look on the plague, after that it is washed: and, behold, if the plague have not changed his colour, and the plague be not spread; it is unclean; thou shalt burn it in the fire; it is fret inward, whether it be bare within or without. 56 And if the priest look, and, behold, the plague be somewhat dark after the washing of it; then he shall rend it out of the garment, or out of the skin, or out of the warp, or out of the woof: 57 And if it appear still in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in any thing of skin; it is a spreading plague: thou shalt burn that wherein the plague is with fire. 58 And the garment, either warp, or woof, or whatsoever thing of skin it be, which thou shalt wash, if the plague be departed from them, then it shall be washed the second time, and shall be clean. 59 This is the law of the plague of leprosy in a garment of woollen or linen, either in the warp, or woof, or any thing of skins, to pronounce it clean, or to pronounce it unclean.”
Garments too may be infected with leprosy. A person's clothes signify his conduct, so it must be pure in his appearance, his speech and his behavior.
Warp: the lengthwise threads of the fabric.
Woof: the crosswise threads of the fabric.

The spot carrying the infection may appear in the lengthwise or crosswise threads of the fabric of the garment, whether wool or linen, and it appears also in the garment or article of skin, and its color tends to greenish or reddish. Then the garment is shown to the priest.
The priest examines the garments. If he finds in them the symptoms mentioned above, he isolates them for seven days; and if the plague spreads, the garment is leprous and unclean.
The priest burns the garment because it is unclean and to prevent the spread of infection, and this signifies cutting off sin and keeping away from it completely, whatever the loss.
Any thing: that is, articles made of skin.
If the plague has not spread, the priest has it washed and isolates the garment for another week.
Fret: a hole or erosion.
Bare: the worn place in the cloth.

If the plague has not spread but its appearance remains as it was and has not disappeared with washing, and this is clear after the garment has dried, the garment is considered unclean and must be burned. The infection will have caused a hole or erosion, whether on the inside of the garment or the outside. This signifies the need for continued repentance in order to cut off any traces of sin.

But if the color of the infection remains dark after washing, the priest tears out only the area of the plague, out of care not to spoil and lose the whole garment; but it is torn out lest it turn into leprosy afterward. This signifies being on guard against what leads to sin and keeping away from it.
Spreading: living leprosy that breeds and increases.
If the infection reappears in the garment, it is then of the living kind that can spread, so the whole garment is burned.

But if the plague disappears after washing, it was merely a spot, so the garment is washed again to confirm its cleanness and then used again because it is clean. Thus one must guard against every appearance of evil.
Such is the law concerning the leprosy of garments.

Would that you were careful about your conduct and appearance, and even about every word you utter and every word you hear, lest by hearing it repeatedly it makes you fall into sin. And do not forget that you will give an account on the Day of Judgment for every idle word. In this way you keep yourself pure from every evil and every appearance of evil.
The cleansing of the leper and leprosy of houses: introduction

To show the hideousness of sin so that man may hate it, the leper is isolated, because his disease signifies uncleanness, and he stays outside the camp, away from the people, until he repents, and then God heals him, since he has no medical cure. Then he needs three stages for his cleansing, so that he may feel the importance of the new, pure life that he will receive, hold fast to it and keep away from every sin. These steps of cleansing signify the redemption that Christ accomplished on the Cross and gave us in the Church and her sacraments.
(a) The cleansing of the leper (vv. 1-20). It includes three stages, which are:

God commands that anyone who offers one of his children as a human sacrifice to the god Molech, the god of the children of Ammon, out of fear of him, shall be put to death. This sin was mentioned in (ch. 18:21), but here the punishment is stated, which is death by stoning. This is carried out either by striking him with stones until he dies, or by binding him and throwing him down from a height onto a large stone and placing another large stone on his chest until he dies.

God declares His anger against the man who gave one of his children to the pagan god Molech, and decrees that He will destroy him, because by this deed he has defiled the sanctuary of God, which is His house and His people; that is, he has offended and defied God by this great evil.
If the clan of this wicked man cooperates with him and hides him, out of fear for him or of him, they thereby help him in his evil, so God declares that He will destroy him and destroy them.

Do not cover up sin, for by this you encourage it and make the wicked persist in it. Be strong and proclaim the truth, and care about the salvation of the souls around you; but present the word of God in the manner suited to the one to whom you present it, so that you may draw his heart to the fear of God and he may turn back from his evil.
Here God also decrees the punishment of whoever deals with mediums, sorcerers, familiar spirits and all who deal with demons: that he must perish and die. This sin was mentioned in (ch. 19:31).

Finally God commands them and warns them about the life of holiness in which they ought to live, because He is holy. If they are His people, they must be holy to Him, that is, they must not worship any god other than Him and must keep away from all pagan practices, and, on the other hand, they must keep His commandments and apply them in their lives.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: His blood shall be upon him: he shall be put to death.

The fifth commandment, as well as the Law (ch. 19:3), requires the honoring of parents. But whoever does not respect them, and instead dishonors them and insults them with cursing, does not respect God, nor those who are older than himself, foremost among whom are his parents; he has not appreciated their labors in his birth and upbringing. He is ungrateful, and therefore God commands that he be put to death.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: God declares the punishment for adultery with a married woman, which is death, carried out by stoning (Deut 22:22). But if she is a virgin, he marries her and pays a fine (Deut 22:28, 29). For adultery with a married woman is an assault on the oneness of the marriage and on the belonging of each to the other, whereas in the second case it is possible to marry her as a remedy for the wrong, and he is punished by paying a fine because he assaulted her and did not marry her like the other girls.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: Whoever dares to commit adultery with his father's wife must be put to death, whether he did this during his father's lifetime or after his death, because his father's wife stands in the place of his mother; he has assaulted motherhood and defied God.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: Whoever commits adultery with his daughter-in-law must be put to death, because he did not respect his fatherhood toward her, and through his lust he has set himself against God and against all values.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: Whoever falls into sexual perversion by having a physical relationship with a male has burned with his lust against all the natural laws that God created. He is like an animal in his lust and must be put to death.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: If a man marries a woman and her daughter at the same time, or marries the mother and then the daughter, or the reverse, that is, the daughter and then the mother, whether during the lifetime of both or after the death of one of them, he has assaulted motherhood by his marriage to the girl's mother, and daughterhood by his marriage to the mother's daughter, and so he must be put to death.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: Their blood shall be upon them: there is no sin upon whoever kills them, because they deserve it.

This base sin, adultery with animals, was spoken of before in (ch. 18:23), and the punishment was the death of the man or woman who committed it, and of the animal, not because the animal had sinned, but to be rid of every trace of evil and uncleanness.

If you have sinned by adultery in any form, whether in word or deed, in any manner, do not be content with repentance, confession and Holy Communion alone. Keep away also, as far as you can, from everything associated with the sin, from persons and places, and get rid of any pictures or belongings that remind you of the sin, so that you begin a new, pure page with God.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: Whoever marries his sister, whether his full sister or his half-sister, is punished by being cut off from the people of God, because he did not preserve the purity of the relationship between brothers and sisters.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: The fountain of her blood: her reproductive organs from which the blood flows.

If a man has a physical relationship with his wife during her monthly period, or during her illness with a disease that causes her to bleed, and does so deliberately and not by oversight (ch. 15:24, 18:19), both of them are punished by being cut off from the people of God, because they indulged in lust even though the woman's health condition did not suit such a union.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: He also warns against marrying a maternal or paternal aunt, because she is among the relatives whom it is forbidden to marry (ch. 18:12, 13, ch. 18:6). If two dare to enter into this wrong relationship, they bear the guilt of this sin and its punishment, which is being cut off from the people of God.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: If a man marries his uncle's wife, he has transgressed the law of forbidden marriages, for she stands in the place of his aunt, that is, his mother. They bear the punishment of this sin, which is most likely being cut off from the people of God, in addition to their becoming childless, and this means:
1- God strikes them with barrenness, so that they have no children.
2- Or their children born of them die.
3- Or the children born are considered illegitimate, because God is not pleased with this relationship.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: The Law had already declared the prohibition of marrying the wife of a brother, whether during his lifetime if he had divorced her, or after his death if she had borne children (ch. 18:16). If this happens, it is considered a crime and an uncleanness, because he has dishonored his brother, that is, he did not respect the feelings of brotherhood, and their punishment is childlessness, as was explained in the previous verse.

entries.section: (3) By holiness they dwell in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: God reminds them of the importance of keeping His commandments and worshiping Him so that they may remain in the Promised Land, and of not taking part in the worship of idols like the pagan inhabitants of the land, lest this holy land vomit them out, that is, the land which God sanctified by dwelling in it and by their holy worship. Because God hated the evils of the original inhabitants of the land, He drove them out of it and settled the children of Israel in it in their place, because they were distinguished by the worship of God and by holiness, so they received the good things of the land, which is described as flowing with milk and honey.

entries.section: (3) By holiness they dwell in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: God reaffirms to them the law of the foods permitted from clean animals and birds, together with keeping away from eating the unclean animals and birds which He distinguished, that is, defined, for them.

entries.section: (3) By holiness they dwell in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: God demands holiness of them, that is, that they worship Him alone and keep away from all evil, for two reasons:
1- Because He is holy and righteous, and they can live with Him and enjoy fellowship with Him.
2- Because God has distinguished them from the other peoples with many blessings, and therefore they have no need of the pagan gods, who are demons, and of all their evils that corrupt the soul.

Remember, when Satan presents any sin to you, that the holy God, your heavenly Father, is looking at you. Do not defile yourself with sin and separate yourself from Him, so that you are deprived of His blessings, His fellowship and His love. Hold fast to holiness, for it is your means of enjoying peace and joy forever.

entries.section: (3) By holiness they dwell in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: The gravity of the sin of dealing with demons, who are called familiar spirits, and of those who deal with them, who are called sorcerers, was spoken of before (ch. 19:31). If anyone transgresses this commandment and deals with demons, his guilt is great and he is punished by death by stoning.
The Book of Exodus: The holiness of the priests

The Law forbids the priest to take part in the burial rites of any person, because death is connected with sin and is therefore considered an uncleanness, and whoever touches or takes part in the burial of a dead person becomes unclean. The priest is the example of holiness for all the people.
The priest is allowed an exception for seven near relatives, whom he may take part in burying without being defiled, because he is directly responsible for them. These relatives are:
The father, the mother, the son, the daughter, the brother, the unmarried sister, and the wife.

As for the married sister, her husband is responsible for her. As for the wife, as is made clear in (v. 4), he is not defiled by taking part in her burial, because he and she are one flesh, and she is the one referred to as his kin (v. 4). But as for the rest of the kin and relatives, whatever their rank, he must not defile himself by burying them.
He warns them against practices that were offered to the pagan gods, such as:
1- Making a bald spot on the head by shaving all sides of the head and leaving a circle of hair on top of the head.
2- Shaving the hair from the sides of the beard, that is, the two sides, and leaving the middle part on the chin, in order to please the gods.
3- Making cuttings in the various parts of the body.
If the whole people are forbidden to do these pagan practices, how much more the priest, who is their highest example, so that his worship is wholly for God and not for idols.
Here He declares the importance of the holiness of the priests and of their keeping away from burying the dead or from pagan practices, for the following reasons:
1- Because their lives are set apart, consecrated and holy to God.
2- Because they are the highest example for the people in hallowing the name of the Lord, so that the people may follow their example.
3- Because they offer the offerings and burnt offerings to God in His house, and because of their greatness, the one who offers them needs to be holy.

Do not forget that you are holy to God, so give Him your whole heart and not sin and the world. And if you sin, wash your heart by repentance and confession, and sanctify also your thoughts, your words and your deeds, so that you may be an example for others and a light to the world.
The priest represents perfection and is an example for the people, so he must also be careful about his marriage:
1- The wife he chooses must not be known among the people for immorality, lest she return to her immorality and cause the people and her husband to stumble.
2- She must not be defiled by any evil deed well known among the people, such as theft, lest she trouble the priest by her conduct and cause the people to stumble.
3- His wife must not have been married before and divorced, lest the reason for her divorce was bad conduct and she return to it.

God addresses the people and asks them to regard the priest as holy in their eyes, because he offers the offerings of the Lord, and God sanctified him on the day of his ordination. The effect of the people's hallowing of the priest appears in: The Book of Exodus
1- Respecting him.
2- Following his example.

Here He stresses the importance of the priest's taking care in raising his children, because he is an example for the people, and therefore He makes the punishment severe for the priest's daughter if she falls into immorality. If any virgin commits adultery, she is stoned, but the priest's daughter is burned with fire, as a declaration of God's anger against her, to wipe out the stumbling block she could cause the people, and as a declaration of the priest's rejection of this shameful conduct, because her immorality has defiled the house of the priest and become a disgrace and an object of the people's mockery. Her burning with fire confirms the purity of the priest and puts the fear of God in the hearts of the people.

entries.section: (2) The holiness of the high priest

paragraphs.text: The chief priest: the high priest.

In this verse and the following verses God speaks about the high priest, on whose head the oil was poured on the day of his consecration, whose hand was filled, that is, who began to offer the sacrifices, and who put on the splendid garments of the high priest. He is the highest example for the priests and the people, and he is responsible for the care of the priests. So he must not indulge in displays of grief and distress by uncovering his head and tearing his clothes, as some of the people do, because his sorrows have hope, and by his composure he is an example to others.
The high priest is a type of Christ, so he does not uncover his head, that is, his dignity, and does not tear his clothes, which signify the Church.

entries.section: (2) The holiness of the high priest

paragraphs.text: God forbids him to take part in the burial rites of any dead person, even if it is his father or mother. He is an example of purity and of keeping away from any uncleanness, although the ordinary priest is permitted to take part in the burial of the seven near relatives (vv. 2-4).

entries.section: (2) The holiness of the high priest

paragraphs.text: The sanctuary: the tabernacle of meeting.

Here He confirms that the high priest is not to take part in anyone's funeral or in any trouble that requires him to go out from the tabernacle of meeting, because he serves God in His house, and it is not right for him to go out and leave the service, for it is more important than any other worldly work. He supports this by the fact that upon his head are the crowns of glory and honor which he received through the pouring of the oil on his head, so that he may come forward and stand in the presence of God; therefore it is not right for him to leave God for any reason.

entries.section: (2) The holiness of the high priest

paragraphs.text: It is required in the choice of his wife that she be a virgin, for he is a type of Christ, who betrothed the Church to Himself as a virgin, so that all her feelings and her love are for Him.

He does not marry a widow, lest she make a comparison between him and her first husband, which may cause problems. And he does not marry a divorced woman, that is, one who entered into problems with her first husband, so that she may be at peace and suitable for union with this great position of leadership, the position of the high priest.
And he does not marry a woman of immorality who has been defiled by this sin, for she does not suit this great position, which needs great purity.
This virgin must of course be a Jewess, that is, from his own people, because foreign women were associated with the worship of idols; that is, she ought to be a believer in God and live with Him.

entries.section: (2) The holiness of the high priest

paragraphs.text: One of the reasons for the care in choosing the wife is that the high priest may have blessed offspring, not defiled because of the morals and conduct of their mother, so that he does not expose his position of leadership to the talk of the people, or to being a stumbling block for him. In addition, his sons will be priests, and if an impure and careless mother raises them, they will be wicked. God affirms that He has sanctified him and set him apart for His service, so his whole family must be pure and set apart for Him.
The Book of Exodus

Care for the holiness of your home, your wife and your children, by looking after them, showing them love, and binding them to the Church, so that it may be a Christian home that glorifies God, and you may be an example to those around you and enjoy an atmosphere that helps you grow spiritually.

Here He mentions the physical conditions that must be met by the priest so that he may be without blemish, for he is a type of Christ, the Lamb without blemish, and so that his permanent defect may not hinder him from the service of God. This applies throughout the service of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levites "in their generations", that is, it is not applied in the New Testament, because these physical defects signify spiritual defects; if the latter, the spiritual ones, are found in the New Testament, he is barred from the priesthood.

Here He specifies the physical defects that bar from the priesthood. They are not applied in the New Testament, but if a disability exists that prevents the priest from carrying out his service, in that case he is barred only from the priesthood. The grounds for exclusion in the Old Testament are:
1- A blind man: this signifies the lack of spiritual insight and spiritual understanding.
2- A lame man: this signifies the uprightness lacking in his conduct.
3- One who has a flat nose: that is, one with a deformity of the nose, so that he cannot distinguish well by smell; this signifies weakness in distinguishing between right and wrong.
4- One who has anything superfluous: that is, one who has any excess growth on his body, such as an extra finger; this signifies excessive preoccupation with the world.

5- One who has a broken foot or broken hand: this would hinder him from performing his service, and it appears that the setting of fractures at that time was not completely possible; it signifies weakness in the capacity for spiritual work and sound conduct.
6- Crookbackt: that is, one with a bowed back, and this prevents him from performing the service successfully. It signifies one burdened with the load of many sins on his back who does not feel them.

7- A dwarf: that is, one from whom some part of his body is missing, such as the nose or a finger. The dwarf is counted as one of its kinds, and this hinders him from his service and signifies the person who is lacking in his spiritual relationship with God.
8- One who has a blemish in his eye: this is a white cloud that obscures sight and signifies weakness in spiritual discernment.
9- Scurvy: this is one who has a skin disease that makes him inclined to scratch. It signifies one on whom the marks of sin appear and who causes others to stumble.
10- Scabbed: this is one who has patches differing from the color of the skin on his face and on some parts of his body. It signifies one whose life sin disfigures and who causes others to stumble.

11- Having his stones broken: this is one to whom an accident has happened, or who was struck on his testicles, or who has a disease that weakens them. It signifies spiritual weakness and preoccupation with lusts.

In conclusion, God affirms that the priest should have no physical defects, so that they do not hinder him from his service and so that the people may feel that he is perfect, because their outlook in the Old Testament was material. In addition, some of them thought that physical defects were due to sin; this is a mistaken belief, but it existed among them and could confuse their minds concerning the priest and cause him trouble.
The Book of Exodus
The most holy and the holy: the foods that the priest takes from the house of the Lord, which are most holy or holy and set apart for him.

If a priest of the seed of Aaron has a physical defect among the defects mentioned above and is not permitted to serve in the house of the Lord, he is nevertheless not deprived of his portion of the food and drink that the priest receives, because he does no material work that brings him profit, just as the New Testament teaches that the expenses of the priest's life be provided (1 Cor 9:
11-14), even if he is struck by illness or reaches old age, which hinders him from service.

Here He confirms that one who has a defect is not permitted to enter the sanctuary to serve God and to see the veil that separates the sanctuary from the Holy of Holies. Nor may he approach the bronze altar to offer sacrifices, because if he dared and performed a service, he would defile the place by breaking the commandments of God, who sanctified the place and the servants who work in it and barred the one who has a defect from service.

Moses taught Aaron and his sons all the preceding commandments concerning the sanctification of the priests mentioned in this chapter, and likewise taught the people all the commandments of God mentioned in the preceding chapters. He is a faithful servant who carries out his work with care.

Examine yourself to discover your spiritual defects and your weaknesses of soul, then ask for God's help and the guidance of your father of confession to correct them. And know that God is able to forgive your sins, however many they are, and to complete what is lacking in you, whatever you suffer from.
Conditions for the sacrifices offered to God

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Separate themselves: respect and revere.

The holy things of the children of Israel: the foods that the priests eat from the offerings and sacrifices of the children of Israel to God. God asked Moses to teach Aaron and his sons the priests to respect the holy things of God, eating them with fear and reverence and not like the rest of their foods, for in this eating of theirs they perform a divine work, since they proclaim God's acceptance The Book of Exodus of the sacrifices and offerings of the people, and they feel that God is the Giver of this food and its Blesser, so they eat it with joy and humility. For their eating these holy things with greed or with evil desire, as if it were ordinary food, is a defiling and a despising of God.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: To confirm the reverence due from the priests and their households for the Lord's portion of the foods which they eat, He warns them against eating of it if any of them has an uncleanness for any of the reasons mentioned previously in this book. Whoever makes light of it and eats of these foods while his uncleanness is upon him is cut off from the priesthood and deprived of service before God, that is, he is removed far from God, because he has defiled His holy things.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: He gives examples of cases of uncleanness that are barred from eating the holy things of God, which are:
1- The priest who is afflicted with leprosy (ch. 13, 14).
2- The priest who is afflicted with a discharge (ch. 15:1-15).
3- The priest who touches a dead person or something belonging to him (ch. 21).
4- A priest who has had marital relations with his wife (ch. 15:16-18).
5- A priest who has touched an unclean creeping animal, or anything touched by the carcass of that unclean animal (ch. 11:24-44).
6- A priest who has touched an unclean person, with any kind of uncleanness.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: If any priest is made unclean by any of the preceding uncleannesses or by any other kind of uncleanness, he remains unclean until evening, then he washes his whole body, and after that he is permitted to eat of the holy things of God, which are his food.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: All the people were forbidden to eat animals that had died or been torn by beasts, because their blood is in them (ch. 17:15, 16); how much more is the priest not permitted to eat of them, lest he defile himself.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: My ordinance: My worship and My statutes.
God warns His priests to be exacting in applying His Law in their worship of Him; as for whoever makes light of it, he exposes himself to death as the punishment for despising the Law of God.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: The portion of the priests from the sacrifices and offerings of God is eaten by him and his seed, that is, his wife and his children only, and it is not permitted for any of the following to eat of it:
1- Strangers, that is, Jews who are not of the seed of the priests (Num 1:15).
2- Sojourners, that is, guests, whether they are Jews or non-Jews.
3- Hired servants, that is, those who work for the priests, whether temporary slaves or day laborers, Jews or non-Jews.

In sum, these holy foods (such as his portion of the peace offering) are enjoyed only by the priest and his household, as a divine grace with which God favors the priest and his household, and they signify the blessing of God given to the priests and servants.

If you serve God and labor for His sake, know that He is rich and is not indebted to anyone, but He will bless you with many blessings by which you are distinguished from others, not only material blessings but rather spiritual blessings that advance you on the road to the Kingdom; so seize every opportunity to offer Him your love.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Those permitted to eat of the holy things of God, other than the priest's household, are:
1- The slaves whom the priest bought and circumcised, so that they became Jews residing permanently with the priest.
2- Slaves born to male and female slaves who reside permanently in the priest's house; these are circumcised and permitted to eat.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: The priest's daughter eats of the holy things of God, and if she marries a priest she will also eat of them, but if she marries a stranger, that is, a Jew who is not of the priests, she is under his care and belongs to him, and so she is deprived of the food of her father's house, which is the holy things of God.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: It is also permitted to eat of the holy things for the following:
1- The priest's daughter who married a stranger and then he divorced her, so she returned to her father's house.

2- The widow whose stranger husband died and who bore no children by him, so she returned to her father's house. The Book of Exodus But the widow who bore children, whether she returned to her father's house or did not return, does not eat of the holy things, neither she nor her children, because her husband's family are responsible to provide for her.
3- If the widow's children die, she returns to her father's house and is permitted to eat of the holy things.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: If any Jewish person who is not of the seed of the priests eats of the holy things of God by oversight, that is, unintentionally, he has sinned, and he is to do the following:
1- He offers a trespass offering, a ram for God.
2- He gives food like what he ate and adds a fifth to it, as compensation and an apology for his error.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: If some of the people sin and eat by oversight of the holy things of God that are set apart for the priests, or if the priests sin and eat of these holy things while they are unclean, then they:
1- Profane the name of God and do not respect it.
2- Defile the whole people, because they are individuals of it.
This makes a person careful in his worship and conduct, because his sin offends God and his whole family and community, and even encourages others to it, so that he spreads sin among people.

entries.section: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Their freewill offerings: the voluntary offerings other than those the Law prescribes, which are considered an offering of love to God in thanks for His kindnesses.

The conditions of the sacrifice that the Law prescribed were explained in the first chapters of this book, and the children of Israel used to offer additional offerings, such as vows, which are tied to a particular request from God, or freewill offerings, which are offerings of love to Him. God also requires that these be:
1- From the herd, the sheep or the goats, which are the clean animals that the Law prescribed.
2- A male, which signifies strength, so that the best is offered to God.
3- Perfect: that is, without blemish, as a type of Christ, who is without sin and offered Himself as a sacrifice for us on the Cross.

entries.section: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

paragraphs.text: The vow or freewill sacrifice was offered as a peace offering with these preceding conditions, out of love for God and to obtain His pleasure and blessing; but if anyone makes light of these conditions, this is considered making light of God and brings His anger upon him.
Having pustules: one who has pustules, that is, boils.
Spotted: one who has black dots, that is, freckles.
God forbids the offering of a sacrifice that has any blemish, and He specifies these blemishes, which are:
1- Blind.
2- Broken: having any part of its legs or bones broken.
3- One that has a wound, new or old, which left a clear mark.
4- Having pustules, because pustules mar its appearance.
5- Scabbed: one that has been afflicted with scab disease.
6- Spotted: that is, one whose skin has many patches that mar its appearance.
So no sacrifice with these blemishes is to be brought near on the altar of God.

entries.section: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Having anything superfluous: excessive length in one of the bones, or extra fingers.
The Book of Exodus Lacking in his parts: excessive smallness of the body.

It is not permitted to offer one with anything superfluous or one that is lacking in its parts in these sacrifices which the Law prescribes or in vows, but it is permitted in the case of the freewill offering, because it is a gift of love offered to God.

The peace offering and vows must be without blemish, because they signify Christ, but the freewill offering is a gift from man to God and may have small weaknesses, such as having anything superfluous or being lacking in its parts, because it signifies the weakness of man.

entries.section: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Bruised testicles: one whose testicle was struck so that it was damaged.
Crushed: its testicle was ruined by crushing.
Cut: its testicle was removed and cut off.
The Law forbids the offering of an animal whose testicle is damaged as a sacrifice to God, because it signifies the inability to beget, that is, the lack of spiritual fruit.
And God forbids them to castrate animals in any way, since some pagan worship commanded this.

entries.section: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

paragraphs.text: From a stranger's hand: the animals bought from non-Jews.

God forbids them to buy animals that have blemishes, as was mentioned in the preceding verses, in order to offer them as sacrifices to God, so that they may obtain His pleasure with good and perfect sacrifices; for offering blemished sacrifices is making light of God and of His commands.

Give God the best of what you have, whether in time or in material gifts, so that your perfect love for Him may appear; then the house of God will be better than your own house, and you will care for the brethren of the Lord more than you care for yourself, or at least as you care for yourself.

In His commandments to Moses about offering sacrifices, God added that an animal is not to be offered before seven days from its birth, so that it will have enjoyed suckling from its mother during these days, which is important nourishment for the newborn, and so that its mother also may enjoy it and her motherhood be satisfied. To this extent the mercy of God appears in His Law, so that He may teach us kindness to animals, and all the more that we have compassion on our brothers and sisters, human beings. For this reason the Jews did not slaughter an animal to eat it before seven days from its birth.

May you feel the feelings of others around you, and find excuses for them in their errors and shortcomings, and be longsuffering toward them, and provide for their needs before they ask for them. And compassion is to be shown to all, even animals, because a merciful heart is merciful to the great and the small, the rich and the poor, man and animal.

To complete the feelings of mercy, the Law commands that the mother animal not be slaughtered with her young in one day; it is enough that the animal has lost its young or lost its mother, so it is not to be offered for slaughter on the same day, because it is affected by this loss. This is the divine mercy that God expects us to practice with one another, so that we are not harsh to a person and his child at the same time.
The Book of Exodus

If a person offers a thank offering to God, that is, a peace offering, his purpose is to please God and obtain His blessing in his life; therefore he adheres to all the conditions previously mentioned in this book, which mean offering the best that he has, and that it be without blemish.

Here He stresses the importance of eating the peace offering on the same day, as came in (ch. 7:15), for it signifies the sacrifice of the Eucharist in the New Testament, which is eaten on the same day.

At the end of this chapter God asks them to be committed to carrying out His commandments in all their sacrifices, thereby declaring their fear of God and their love for Him, because any violation of His laws is contempt for and defiling of His name before themselves and before the peoples around them. And He reminds them of His love and care for them, for it is He who brought them out of Egypt with great power and preserved them in the wilderness, so they must live for Him and obey His commandments.
The feasts. First: the idea of the feast:
The word feast means a witness or an assembly, and the feasts are called the appointed seasons or religious celebrations, and what is meant by them is:
1- Stopping work and devoting oneself to the worship of God.
2- Remembering important spiritual events that bind people to the worship of God, to loving Him and to thanking Him for His kindnesses.

3- The celebrations in the Old Testament signify Christ the Savior, His redemption and His blessing in our lives, in addition to many spiritual meanings which we will speak about in detail with each feast.
Second: in the New Testament:

Because feasts are a spiritual idea necessary for the spiritual person, they continued in the New Testament also, but their occasions changed, since they came to center on the One signified, who is Christ, in addition to the feasts of the saints who lived their lives in faith in Christ.
Third: the feasts that the Law prescribed:
A- Weekly feasts: this is the Sabbath day (Ex 20:8-11), which the Jews keep as a feast and on which they worship God in their homes.
B- Monthly feasts: these are the beginnings of the months, called the new moons (Num 10:10, 28:11-15), on which they worship God and offer Him offerings, whether for the Temple or for the poor.
C- Yearly feasts, which include:
1- The Feast of the Passover on the fourteenth of the first month (Ex 12).
2- The Feast of Unleavened Bread, which follows the Feast of the Passover, for seven days (Ex 13).
3- The Feast of the Firstfruits on the eighteenth day of the second month, a remembrance of the offering of the first ripe ear of grain.
4- The Feast of Pentecost, called the Feast of Weeks, which falls in the sixth month (Ex 23:16).
5- The Feast of Trumpets, which falls at the beginning of the seventh month (Lev 23:23, 24).
6- The Day of Atonement, which falls on the tenth day of the seventh month (Lev 16).

7- The Feast of Tabernacles, which falls on the fifteenth day of the seventh month (Lev 23:33-36). These months are the months of the religious year, whereas the first of the months of the civil year is the one corresponding to the seventh month of the religious year.
God commanded the carrying out of these feasts in two stages:
The first stage: this is immediately after the giving of the Law in the wilderness of Sinai, and it comprises the feasts of the Sabbath, the Passover, Unleavened Bread, Trumpets and the Atonement.

The second stage: this is after their entry into the land of Canaan, and it comprises the feasts of the Firstfruits, Pentecost and Tabernacles. And God commanded that all the males of the children of Israel appear at His house at three feasts (Ex 23:14-17), which are:
1- The Feast of the Passover.
2- The Feast of Pentecost.
3- The Feast of Tabernacles.
The males represented the whole family, and the woman also was permitted to attend these feasts, and if she did not attend, the male acted on her behalf.
D- Periodic feasts: that is, every several years, and they are:
1- The seventh year (Ex 23:10, 11, Lev 25:1-7).

2- The year of Jubilee, that is, the fiftieth year (Lev 25:8-22). It is to be noted that God commanded these feasts to Moses and he wrote them in the books of Exodus, Leviticus and Numbers. Fourth: feasts added by the Jews: these are according to their historical occurrence, for important events passed in the life of the Jews and they added other feasts, which are:
1- The Feast of the Dedication of Solomon's Temple after he built it, in the seventh month (1 Kgs 8:2).
2- The remembrance of the restoration of the Temple at the hand of Zerubbabel in the twelfth month (Ezra 6:15).
3- The Feast of the Renewal of the Temple, which Judas Maccabeus ordained, on the twenty-fifth of the ninth month, lasting eight days (1 Macc 4:59), (Jn 10:22).
4- The remembrance of the dedication of the Temple of Herod the Great (Jn 2:20).

5- The two feasts of Purim, on the fourteenth and fifteenth of the twelfth month, which Esther and Mordecai ordained in remembrance of God's deliverance of the children of Israel from the plot of Haman (Esth 9:29-32).

6- The day which the Jews ordained in remembrance of Judith's victory over Holofernes, the commander of the armies of the Assyrians, and the deliverance of the children of Israel from him (Jdt 16:31).
7- The feast of the appearance of the holy fire in the days of Nehemiah (2 Macc 1:18).
8- The remembrance of their victory over Nicanor the commander at the hand of Judas Maccabeus on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month (1 Macc 7:48, 49).

According to your estimation: that is, your assessment and approval of the vow so that it accords with the conditions of the Law (vv. 3-8). After Moses, it was the priest who assessed and approved the vow.

A vow is a promise to offer a gift to God if He grants a person his request, or it is an offering of love given in thanksgiving to God for His kindnesses and in striving to cling to God. The promise is either to do something positive or to abstain from something. Vows were made of persons, animals, birds or fields, and in this part he speaks about vows of persons.

The one who declared the vow was the person himself or those responsible for him, such as his parents. It was required that he be free and not a slave, so that he would have the ability to carry out his vow. If a woman made a vow while in her father's house, her father's consent was required, and likewise in her husband's house her husband's consent was necessary. But if she was a widow or divorced and lived alone or with her children, she could declare a vow.

It was also necessary that the vow be declared aloud, so that a person would not doubt the thoughts that had come to him, and that it be made from wealth of honorable source. A vow is voluntary, but if a person makes a vow he must fulfill it (Deut 23:21-23; Eccl 5:4, 5). Vows have been known from ancient times: Jacob vowed to God (Gen 28:20-22); they are also found among the other pagan peoples, as the sailors who were with Jonah vowed (Jon 1:16); and they continue in Christianity, as Paul vowed (Acts 18:18).
A shekel of silver: about 15 grams.
The shekel of the sanctuary: the exact shekel, a sample of which was kept in the house of the Lord, in order to regulate the scales so that they would not be false.

The first kind of vow of persons is the vow of a man aged from twenty to sixty years, which is the period of bodily strength, in which he is enlisted for war. For him fifty shekels of silver are offered, and if he is unable to fulfill his vow, he is consecrated to the service of God.

The offering of silver instead of the person consecrating himself is a symbol of Christ's redemption, because silver is a symbol of the Word of God, that is, Christ, for it is He who redeems the lives of His children.
In Christianity, after the mystery of redemption has been made clear, a person's vowing himself means consecrating his life to God, such as the vow of virginity or the vow of monasticism.

In the case of a female vowed at the same age, that is, from twenty to sixty years, the silver offered for her is only thirty shekels, because her bodily strength, and therefore her ability to serve and work, is less than that of a man, in addition to the woman's responsibilities in caring for her house and her children.
If the person vowed is between five and twenty years of age, his ability to work is less, so for a male twenty shekels are offered and for a female ten shekels.

If the one vowed is a child between one month and five years of age, his service is either nonexistent or very slight, so five shekels are offered for him if he is male, or three if she is female. There are examples of a vow at this age, such as Samuel (1 Sam 1:22-24), Samson (Judg 13:5) and John the Baptist (Lk 1:15).

If the person vowed is more than sixty years old, his effort is less, so for a male fifteen shekels are offered and for a female ten shekels. It is noticeable that the amount of silver for the female has increased here and become two thirds of the man's, because a woman's ability to work in old age is often greater than in the days of childhood.

If the one who vowed is poor and cannot offer the silver in the amounts mentioned above, he stands before the priest, who examines his financial means and determines for him the amount of money that he is able to offer to God. Note the mercy of God, who has compassion on His poor children and rejoices in their gifts even if they are very small.

If you have not vowed your life to God, do not forget that you are wholly His possession, for it is He who redeemed you. So consecrate your heart to love Him, strive to be with Him, and drive out every evil desire that defiles your heart.

B- Of animals (vv. 9-13) 9"And if it be a beast, whereof men bring an offering unto the LORD, all that any man giveth of such unto the LORD shall be holy. 10 He shall not alter it, nor change it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good: and if he shall at all change beast for beast, then it and the exchange thereof shall be holy. 11 And if it be any unclean beast, of which they do not offer a sacrifice unto the LORD, then he shall present the beast before the priest: 12 And the priest shall value it, whether it be good or bad: as thou valuest it, who art the priest, so shall it be. 13 But if he will at all redeem it, then he shall add a fifth part thereof unto thy estimation.
Whereof men bring an offering unto the LORD: that is, of the clean animals that are permitted to be offered as sacrifices to God, namely cattle, sheep and goats.
Holy: set apart for God.

If a person vows to offer one of the animals to God if God grants him his request, he must offer exactly what he vowed and may not substitute anything for it, and it is required that it be one of the animals permitted to be offered to God, that is, clean animals.

Here he stresses the necessity of fulfilling the vow just as its maker pronounced it, and not substituting another animal for it. If he does this, that is, offers another animal, he is obliged to offer the vow also as he pronounced it, that is, to offer two animals: the one he offered first and the one he vowed. The priests could sell these vowed animals to the people who wished to offer sacrifices to God, and the price was placed in the house of the Lord. Offering the very vow that its maker pronounced is a symbol that God knows us by our names and accepts no substitute for our souls, for we have a place in His heart that no one else can fill; His fatherhood loves us and seeks each one of us specifically.

If a person vows one of the unclean animals, such as the donkey, or an animal with a defect, the animal is made to stand before the priest to value it, and the one who vowed pays the price the priest has set into the house of the Lord. This is a symbol that God does not accept an unclean gift from our hands, that is, one that we have obtained from an unlawful source.

If the maker of the vow desires to keep the animal he vowed, this is considered a fault and an excessive desire, so God accepts his vow by the payment of the animal's price, but he adds to it a fifth, because he desired it after he had vowed it to God.

If Christ did not withhold His life from you but gave it for you on the Cross, then do not withhold your life or anything you own, but be ready to offer everything to God as an expression of your love.

C- Of houses (vv. 14, 15) 14"And when a man shall sanctify his house to be holy unto the LORD, then the priest shall estimate it, whether it be good or bad: as the priest shall estimate it, so shall it stand. 15 And if he that sanctified it will redeem his house, then he shall add the fifth part of the money of thy estimation unto it, and it shall be his.
If a person vows his house to God, the priest values its price, the priest sells it, and he offers its price to the house of God.
If the one who vowed his house to God desires to keep his house, this is considered an excessive desire, and therefore he pays the price of the house and also a fifth in addition.

If the priest was the voice of God in the Old Testament, to guide the people and assess their life, how much more in the New Testament, through the sacrament of confession, in which God declares His voice to you through the tongue of your father of confession. So present your life before him in repentance, and pray to God, and He will guide you through the tongue of the priest, and you will rejoice in God's leading of your life.
